source: YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-22:40 (tools/video_draft.py transcript pdITCHUnEa8 --start 0 --end 1360), card names corrected against data/Sets/FRA_PremierDraft_All_Data.json; nothing past 22:40 read. 'type' marks each idea as claim, heuristic or one-off pick; 'repeats' lists ideas of earlier videos it restates; 'related' lists looser topic matches.

ideas.claim: Stingcaster Mage is a great two-for-one (enters, flashes back an instant or sorcery) and is taken over the rare Liliana the Faultless in P1p1; Liliana was strong against him only because of a Lyra angel deck.
ideas.quote: I think Stingcaster Mage is great. It enters and floods you flashback in his inner sorcery.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and ALSA of Stingcaster Mage against Liliana the Faultless; within-deck value by number of instants and sorceries.

ideas.claim: Sideboard-quality cards (Arcane Amphisbaena, Way of the Necromancer) are never really playable main-deck; they are cards you see in post-board games.
ideas.quote: These kind of sideboard cards are like never playable really outside of this like postboard games
ideas.test_idea: Main-deck play rate and GIH WR of Arcane Amphisbaena and Way of the Necromancer.

ideas.claim: Early in pack 1 take the bigger body without committing to a colour: Marwyn, the Preserver (2-mana 3/2) over the two-drop Skilled Battlecarver, 'trying not to bias too much'.
ideas.quote: I just kind of like getting stats out there. Not trying to bias too much
ideas.test_idea: Early-pick value of a mono-coloured stats card against a flexible two-drop, by pick number.

ideas.claim: Marwyn, the Clearcutter is only an aggro 2-for-1 and he does not prioritise it: you rarely want to sacrifice a land and there are few artifacts. (Later he takes it as a late-game engine next to two Marwyn the Preservers.)
ideas.quote: I don't like prioritizing it too highly because you don't usually end up in spots where you feel good sacrificing a land and there's not a ton of artifacts running around.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Marwyn, the Clearcutter by deck artifact count.

ideas.claim: Easiest No Admittance of his life at P1p7: he has been trying to play Eye of Jace, but No Admittance is the easy pick, good with Stingcaster Mage.
ideas.quote: Easiest no admittance of my life.
ideas.test_idea: ALSA and GIH WR of No Admittance against Eye of Jace.

ideas.claim: Wrath of the Bloodmane is really good with Stingcaster Mage and cheap because of the legendary creatures already in the pool; cheap legends make the cost reduction work.
ideas.quote: Wrath of the blood mane really good with stinger caster mage. It's a cheap card. I already have some cheap legendaries to go with it.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of Wrath of the Bloodmane by number of legendary creatures in the deck.

ideas.claim: Heartstring Puller over Tetsuko Umezawa, Pursuer: Tetsuko is better if it lives, but Puller is the better card; red looks wide open from the packs wheeling.
ideas.quote: Tetsuko is like if it lives, it's better than the Polar, but Polar is just a better card. And red looks wide open in this draft.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Heartstring Puller against Tetsuko Umezawa, Pursuer.

ideas.claim: Speculating on a card that was not taken over anything good is free: Tetsuko Umezawa, Fugitive at P1p12 and the blue-red land at P1p13 cost nothing, and he keeps blue as an option.
ideas.quote: I think here was probably fine. I mean, we weren't passing up much.
ideas.test_idea: Late-pick speculation value: win rate of last-picked cards by colour that ends up in the deck.

ideas.claim: Some formats reward bobbing and weaving and some reward finding a lane; here he stays flexible (red definite, green or blue second) and keeps speculative cards in a pile.
ideas.quote: Sometimes it's about bobbing and weaving. Some formats really reward you for just finding a lane, sticking to it
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of decks that changed second colour after pick 8 against decks that did not.

ideas.claim: Take the swingy bomb over the on-plan grind card: a card like Lyra that must be answered wins a game or two over a run, whereas Tetsuko and Heartstring Puller grind and lose to a Lyra you cannot answer.
ideas.quote: having a card like Lyra is going to win me like one or two games over the course of my run potentially
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of decks with a must-answer rare against decks without, controlling for skill.

ideas.claim: Ruric Thar, Biomagus over Frostbite Pyromental: a giant flier is better than a hard-to-cast four-damage-and-draw-two card that does not help attack planeswalkers.
ideas.quote: I think the giant flyer might be better.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Ruric Thar, Biomagus against Frostbite Pyromental.

ideas.claim: Draconic Visitor is a fine five-mana 5/5 flier even with no artifact tokens: 'you don't need the extra text to be relevant'; taken over Awaken the Inferno.
ideas.quote: It's also just a five five for five flying anyway. So we're going to take it for sure over awaken the inferno.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Draconic Visitor by number of Heartwood or artifact token makers in the deck.

ideas.claim: Undulating Witness is 'kind of terrible'; he takes it over Rockfall Vale only as a green splash hedge, and does not want to splash the blue-green or red-green cards.
ideas.quote: An undulating witness doesn't seem terrible. I mean, it doesn't seem great. It actually does seem kind of terrible
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Undulating Witness against the other basic landcyclers.

ideas.claim: Traxos, Academy Guardian is a very strong card: annoying at four mana, scary cast alongside a three-drop on turn five.
ideas.quote: Traxxas is so sweet. You even just cast him for four is pretty annoying.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Traxos, Academy Guardian.

ideas.claim: Hapatra, the Desert Frost is better than Chandra's Emberling: a four-mana 4/3 that taps their permanents buys a lot of time and can give pseudo-haste.
ideas.quote: I think this card is just way better though. 4 three buys you a lot of time by tapping their stuff.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Hapatra, the Desert Frost against Chandra's Emberling.

ideas.claim: A curve into Protege's Awakening is strong in a deck with Lyra: Lyra into Awakening draws three cards in a turn and makes a 3/3 angel; the synergy justifies a fifth four-drop.
ideas.quote: You curve Lyra into the uh awakening and then immediately draw a card and then you've drawn three cards and you get another three three
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of Protege's Awakening with Lyra in the deck; draws per turn.

ideas.claim: Frostbite Pyromental over Cryotheory Adept: the Adept needs non-creature spells and the deck has few.
ideas.quote: I don't have that many non-creatures.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Cryotheory Adept by number of noncreature spells.

ideas.claim: Craftwork Crusher still coming around at pick 11 shows red-green would have been open and would have paid off; he is committed to blue-red anyway.
ideas.quote: the fact that craft work crusher is still coming around is crazy. We're we're committed at this point.
ideas.test_idea: ALSA of Craftwork Crusher; later-pick appearances as a signal for the colour pair.

ideas.claim: Fulminous Forte is good but not great in a creature-heavy deck: it needs non-creature spells and surveil for Proft, but an instant-speed removal spell is worth taking and flashes back with Stingcaster Mage.
ideas.quote: Another good instant speed removal spell is going to be great for our deck.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Fulminous Forte by number of noncreature spells in the deck.

ideas.claim: Sphinx of False Conclusions is 'messed up' and a near-forced take at P3p3 over No Admittance, Unsummon and Heartstring Puller, with the expectation that the others wheel (No Admittance did wheel).
ideas.quote: I think this card is just messed up, so we got to take it pretty much.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Sphinx of False Conclusions; wheel rate of No Admittance at pick 11.

ideas.claim: With a high curve, tempo (Unsummon) was tempting, but another kill spell (Wrath of the Bloodmane) is the pick; at six or so removal spells he is comfortable.
ideas.quote: Maybe I am supposed to just take Wrath. Let's get another kill spell.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate by removal count in UR decks; Unsummon against Wrath of the Bloodmane in pick order.

ideas.claim: Variable Chaser over a cheap two-drop (Eardrum Rattler): the two-drop is 'much worse', take the high-quality 2/3 flying prowess body.
ideas.quote: Let's just take the high quality card, the prowess creature.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Variable Chaser against Eardrum Rattler.

ideas.claim: A guaranteed kill spell (Awaken the Inferno #2) over finicky cards (Fblthp, Impossibly Lost) when he already has two Wraths.
ideas.quote: I'd rather just get a good kill spell. Guaranteed.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Awaken the Inferno against Fblthp, Impossibly Lost.

ideas.claim: Twinned Vision is really good in a deck with discard outlets; one copy, and the two-drop (Eardrum Rattler) is not needed once two-drops came back.
ideas.quote: I think one twin division is really good in this sort of deck. I have some ways to discard it.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Twinned Vision by number of discard outlets.

ideas.claim: The red cards wheel in this table: No Admittance at pick 11 'is huge' and Frostbite Pyromental also wheels; he expects red to flow from the right.
ideas.quote: Oh my gosh, we got no admittance to come around. That's huge.
ideas.test_idea: Wheel rate of No Admittance at pick 11 or later against its ALSA.

ideas.claim: Build technique: start from the end and work backwards, adding the bombs first (both Sphinxes, Stingcaster Mage, Lyra), then good removal, then the curve fillers.
ideas.quote: This is going to be a deck, I think, where I start from the end and work my way backward.
ideas.test_idea: Compare the builder's deck with a premium-first build on mock pools.

ideas.claim: Add a two-drop when the two-drop slot is thin: three creatures he wants on turn two plus Skilled Battlecarver; four two-drops plus two No Admittances are 'maybe good enough'.
ideas.quote: My two drop slot has three creatures in it that I want to cast on turn two now. So, let's add skilled battle carver.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate by two-drop count in UR decks.

ideas.claim: Play one Infinite Coursework early in the build, then cut it for an aggressive threat: with all the No Admittances he does not need more removal and wants to pressure the opponent.
ideas.quote: I have all these no admittances that do something very similar. And I want to make sure I have enough ways to pressure them.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of Infinite Coursework and Way of the Warlord by removal count.

ideas.claim: Protege's Awakening is cut for a prowess flier because it is the deck's only Empower Jace card besides the No Admittances, so there is little reason to protect Jaces.
ideas.quote: It is kind of my only empower Jace card other than the no admittances though.
ideas.test_idea: Protege's Awakening win rate by number of Empower Jace cards.

ideas.claim: A 12-creature count is too low for this deck, so he adds another threat (Jiang Yanggu, Alone) in the last slot.
ideas.quote: I only have 12 creatures now.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate by creature count in UR decks.
